summary: Intermittent p99 timeouts for streaming sessions during sustained low-per-connection QPS
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using streaming websocket sessions experience intermittent p99 inference timeouts (client sees connection-level timeout / aborted stream) when per-connection QPS is low but overall connection count is sustained.

Impact:
- Multiple NoteStream customers reported degraded UX: streaming responses occasionally stall for 7-10s then timeout at the client.
- Affects interactive use-cases (real-time transcription, chat) with many concurrent low-throughput connections.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) on Dedicated pool dedicated-nylon-03.
- Models: redwood-mini-3b (primary), fallback to redwood-2b.
- Rolling upgrade to runtime v3.8.1 started 2026-03-08, customer observed regressions 2026-03-09 morning.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Establish ~1200 concurrent websocket streaming sessions to the hosted endpoint from many distinct client IPs.
2) Each connection issues a short request stream (1-3 tokens per second, bursty) with long-lived session semantics.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency for token responses and occasional stream disconnects/timeouts.

Observed behavior:
- p50 stable, p95 shows modest increase, p99 spikes to 6-12s intermittently.
- Affected sessions often show a long wait in server-side traces inside the batcher wait loop before execution.
- Some 499/499-like client aborts correlate with timeouts in streaming proxy logs.

Expected behavior:
- Continuous-batcher should dispatch small batches promptly for streaming sessions to maintain low tail latency even at low per-connection QPS.

Initial logs / evidence:
- Streaming proxy (proxy-7) logs: repeated entries of "connection-id=<id> downstream-timeout after 9s" at same time windows.
- Serving runtime trace: request queued in batch-window for 5.8s before dispatch.
- Metrics: continuous-batcher.batch_size distribution shifted lower; batch-window wait_time histogram shows heavy tail.
- No obvious GPU saturation; utilization ~40% on affected nodes.

Hypothesis:
- A change in the run-time v3.8.1 modified the batcher idle aggregation heuristic (aimed to reduce tiny-batch churn). Under sustained high connection count but low per-connection QPS, the heuristic increases the internal hold time for prefix coalescing which inadvertently amplifies tail latency for streaming sessions.

Temporary mitigation suggested to customer:
- Route streaming websocket traffic to a dedicated routing rule that pins to a lower-batching-enabled node pool (workaround applied for NoteStream on 2026-03-10).

Next steps planned:
- Engineering to reproduce at scale in staging with configured client emulator.
- Instrument additional traces in batcher to capture hold_time decision inputs.
- Evaluate reverting the heuristic change or exposing it as a tunable for Dedicated customers.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Support: Confirmed multiple incoming reports from NoteStream with identical pattern; created ticket and added to priority queue.
2026-03-10 - SRE: Captured flame graphs and queue histograms; no node-level CPU/mem/GPU pressure observed.
2026-03-11 - Eng (Liam Chen): Reproduced locally using 1.2k websocket clients; confirmed batcher hold_time increased under v3.8.1 compared to v3.7.4.

2026-03-11 - Eng: Narrowed root cause to a new adaptive_idle_alpha (introduced in runtime v3.8.1) that biases towards larger coalescing windows when observed inter-arrival variance is high across connections.
2026-03-11 - Eng: Crafted hotfix that exposes adaptive_idle_alpha as per-pool configuration and reduces default alpha for streaming-optimized pools.
2026-03-12 - QA: Ran a canary deployment of hotfix in us-east with NoteStream workload; p99 regressions no longer reproducible in 6-hour soak.
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-10: Customer reports intermittent streaming timeouts around 09:20-10:45 EDT. Collected client-side logs and sample connection IDs. Marking P1 due to customer-impacting UX for interactive product.

SRE (Marcos Rivera) 2026-03-10: Uploaded batcher histograms and node metrics to support artifacts: /slack/archives/#support and linked Grafana panels. No saturation; suspect batching policy change in last runtime.

Engineer (Liam Chen) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with emulator. Observed that adaptive_idle_alpha increased hold windows under our test pattern. Will prepare patch to expose per-pool alpha and run canary.
Customer (NoteStream, Emma Zhou) 2026-03-11: Thanks — appreciate the quick diagnosis. We confirmed degraded UX during our morning traffic ramp. Happy to test canary routing as suggested.

Engineer (Liam Chen) 2026-03-12: Hotfix deployed to dedicated-nylon-03 as a canary: adaptive_idle_alpha lowered from 0.8 -> 0.35 for streaming pool. Observed p99 drop from ~9s to ~200ms in test harness. Rolling to remaining nodes now.

Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-03-12: Customer confirmed resolution in production: no further streaming timeouts during a 24h observation window. Closing ticket and scheduling follow-up to add opt-in streaming-optimized routing config to Dedicated docs.
resolution: Hotfix deployed: exposed and lowered adaptive_idle_alpha for streaming-optimized pools; routed NoteStream to streaming-optimized pool. Post-deploy canary showed p99 tail latency reduced to acceptable levels. Follow-up: document per-pool batching tunables and add an automated detection alert for streaming tail increases.
postmortem_actions: Add runbook step: how to pin streaming traffic to streaming-optimized pools
Expose adaptive_idle_alpha in Dedicated console UI as a tunable per pool
Create alert: continuous-batcher tail-latency delta > 2s for 5m
Backfill tests: integration test for many low-qps websocket clients during CI gating
